cards.title: Introduction to Flask Routing
cards.content:
Routing in Flask refers to binding a URL to a Python function. When a user visits a specific URL, Flask executes the corresponding view function and returns the result.

from flask import Flask
app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/')
def home():
    return 'Hello, World!'

content.question: Which Flask decorator is used to bind a function to a URL route?

cards.title: Dynamic Routing and Variables
cards.content:
You can add variable sections to a URL by marking sections with <variable_name>. Your function receives the value as a keyword argument.

@app.route('/user/<username>')
def show_user_profile(username):
    return f'User {username}'

Flask also supports converters like <int:user_id> and <float:price>.

content.text: To specify that a route parameter named id must strictly be an integer, you define it in the route decorator as @app.route('/item/<___:id>')

cards.title: Handling HTTP Methods
cards.content:
By default, a route only answers to GET requests. You can use the methods argument on the route() decorator to handle different HTTP methods.

from flask import request

@app.route('/login', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def login():
    if request.method == 'POST':
        return 'Logging in...'
    else:
        return 'Login form'

cards.title: Match HTTP Methods to Use Cases
URL Building with url_for()
cards.content:
Flask provides the url_for() function to build URLs for a specific function. This avoids hardcoding URLs in your templates and code.

from flask import url_for

@app.route('/')
def index():
    return 'Index Page'

with app.test_request_context():
    print(url_for('index')) # Output: /
    print(url_for('show_user_profile', username='John')) # Output: /user/John

steps: Import url_for from the flask module
Ensure you are within an active request context
Call url_for passing the view function name as the first argument
Pass any necessary dynamic URL variables as keyword arguments

cards.title: Redirects and Errors
cards.content:
To redirect a user to another endpoint, use the redirect() function. To abort a request early with an error code, use abort().

from flask import abort, redirect, url_for

@app.route('/')
def index():
    return redirect(url_for('login'))

@app.route('/restricted')
def restricted():
    abort(401)

content.question: What is the primary benefit of using url_for() instead of hardcoding URL strings?

options.text: It makes the server run faster.
It prevents broken links if URL patterns change later.
It allows handling POST requests automatically.
